name: time_logs
title: Time Logs
description: Work time against tasks. A running timer is a row with is_running true and no ended_at. Server-enforced by /timers/start, /timers/stop, /timers/running (62 - Timer, plan/vocabulary/62-timer-spec.md) -- see packages/app-timers/objects/site/timer_actions.py. v4 makes an entry billable: consulting hours are a usage metric with an APPROVAL GATE, and that gate is the only structural difference between time-and-materials billing and metered cloud billing -- both then run the same meter -> rate -> line -> invoice spine. status walks draft -> submitted -> approved -> billed, and the rate is STAMPED at approval from rate_cards (docs/logic-decisions.md #1), so a rate change next quarter can never reprice work somebody already approved. An approved or billed entry is frozen: correcting it is a compensating entry or a credit on the invoice, never an edit to the evidence of what happened (#5, #8).

fields.name: project_id
fields.label: Project
fields.help: What the hours are billed against. Also half of the rate-card lookup: a rate scoped to this project beats the house default.

fields.name: billable
fields.label: Billable
fields.help: Time worth recording is not always time worth charging for. Unbillable hours still count toward a project's cost -- they are simply never rated.

fields.name: status
fields.label: Status
fields.help: Only the person who logged the time may submit it, and only somebody else's hand moves it to approved -- an approval you can grant yourself is not an approval. rejected returns to draft so the hours can be corrected and resubmitted rather than lost. approved -> billed is machine-advanced by the invoice generator; billed is terminal, because a disputed hour is a credit on the invoice, not a rewind.

fields.name: hourly_rate_cents
fields.label: Rate
fields.help: Stamped at approval from the rate card in force on the day the work happened. Once stamped it belongs to this entry -- later rate changes never reprice approved work.

fields.name: amount_cents
fields.label: Amount
fields.help: Stamped alongside the rate: round(billable seconds / 3600 * rate), half-up, once. The entry is what a client disputes, so it is the thing whose arithmetic they can reproduce.

fields.name: rate_card_id
fields.label: Rate Card
fields.help: Which card was chosen. Keeps 'why am I being charged this?' answerable years later.

fields.name: invoice_id
fields.label: Invoice
fields.help: Stamped when the entry is billed. An entry already carrying one is never billed again -- that is what makes re-running the generator safe.

fields.name: duration_seconds
fields.label: Duration (seconds)
fields.help: Stamped by the stop verb: floor(ended_at - started_at). Never client-writable in practice -- omitted from forms.default, not schema read_only (update_collection_record has no preserve_read_only escape hatch; see packages/app-invoices/objects/system/invoice_totals.py for the same finding and the same workaround).
